# isNonNegative

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is a number that is not negative.</link-summary>

<web-summary>isNonNegative() — Checks whether a value is a number that is not negative. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/number</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function isNonNegative(value: unknown): value is number;
```

`NaN` does not qualify: it is a number, but it is neither negative nor non-negative. The infinities behave as their sign suggests, so `Infinity` qualifies and `-Infinity` does not.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description         |
| :-------- | :-------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `unknown` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is a number that is not negative; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `number` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
isNonNegative(0); // => true
isNonNegative(-0); // => true
isNonNegative(42); // => true
isNonNegative(Infinity); // => true
isNonNegative(-1); // => false
isNonNegative(NaN); // => false
isNonNegative("1"); // => false
```
